newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Angolan inflation falls to 4 percent - central bank.
newsitem.headline: Angolan inflation falls to 4 percent - central bank.

text.p: Inflation in Angola, recovering from two decades of civil war, has dropped sharply in recent months and is estimated to be down to four percent in the first half of September, a senior Angolan official said on Tuesday.

"The first result of the policies of the new government was a dramatic reduction in the inflation rate to nine percent in August from 84 percent in May," Antonio Graca, deputy governor of the Bank of Angola, told reporters in Lisbon.
"Preliminary estimates indicate that the inflation rate in the first 17 days of September was four percent," he added.
Graca said the sharp reduction in inflation was the result of austere policies imposed by the new government appointed by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos in June.

President Dos Santos appointed the government led by Prime Minister Fernando Franca Van Dunem in order to tackle an economic crisis marked by a shortage of basic goods and annual inflation then running at nearly 4,000 percent.
Graca was attending a meeting of central bank governors from Portuguese-speaking countries.
